sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, language 577 'Massalat' (citing Connell 2007 in Brenzinger ed. Language Diversity Endangered pp. 163-178, and Moseley ed. 2010 UNESCO Atlas) (Wayback 2025-08-06)
sources.note: Vitality only: 'Severely endangered... 10 Native speakers worldwide' (Connell 2007); 'Critically endangered... 10... DATE OF INFO 1991' (UNESCO). Bibliography tab lists no descriptive work.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record mass1262 'Massalat' (meds: Ibrahim 1980 'grammar'; Le Rouvreur 1962; Davies 1957; Davies 1924) and family pages maba1274/1275/1276
sources.note: Bibliographic only. The single 'grammar' (Ibrahim, Yahia Al-Rahman 1980, Contribution to some aspects of the description of the Masalit language) is a 'computerized assignment' to [mass1262] and is by its title a description of Masalit (mls), not Massalat; Davies 1924 'The Masalit Sultanate' and Davies 1957 are likewise Masalit/ethnographic. Le Rouvreur 1962 is an ethnography ('Massalat de l'ouest').

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2023. Ethnologue 26th ed., free summary page for Massalat [mdg] (Wayback 2023-03-09)
sources.note: 'Massalat is an endangered indigenous language of Chad... Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by the elderly only.' No linguistic content.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan. Draft circulated for discussion, Cambridge, 10 January 2021 (rogerblench.info, Wayback copy)
sources.note: Table 1 'Basic data on the Maba languages' lists 'Masalat' (Batha region, Oum Hadjer; Ouaddai, Am Dam) with population '? extinct. Ethnic population ca. 25,000' and no dialects or data; sec. 4 Phonology and 4.3 Tones (p. 8) treat Maba and Aiki only ('Lukas (1953) and Caprile (1977) both mark tones and Weiss (2009) concludes that a system of High, Low, Rising and Falling can be established for Maba'). No Massalat forms, no stress statement for any Maban language.

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G., Jr. (ed.). 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th ed. Dallas: SIL International, entry 'Massalat' (web edition, Wayback 2007)
sources.note: 'Population 10 (1991 R. Blench). Ethnic population: 29,836 (1993 census). Region East Batha Prefecture, Oum Hadjer Subprefecture, and Ouaddai Prefecture, Am Dam Subprefecture. Classification Nilo-Saharan, Maban, Mabang, Masalit. Language use Speakers are shifting to Chadian Arabic. Comments The Massalat originally separated from the Masalit along the Sudan border and moved west. Muslim. Nearly extinct.' Nothing on phonology.
